prompt: A logger stores 5 samples at 10 samples per second, starting at zero. What is the last timestamp?

options.explanation: This is the record duration, one sample period after the last timestamp.
Correct. The last sample has index 4, so it occurs four periods after the first.
The rate is ten samples per second; a sample is not one second.

workedExample:
```formula
t = (5 − 1) / (10 / s)
t = 0.4 s
where
t: final timestamp relative to the first sample, in seconds (s)
s: second, the unit of time
In words: Five samples contain four gaps; each gap lasts one tenth of a second.
```

link.title: Primary source: The Scientist and Engineer’s Guide to DSP

prompt: You need a one-second record at 8 samples per second, with the endpoint excluded. Which description is right?

options.explanation: Including both endpoints adds a ninth sample and changes the stated record duration.
Eight samples starting at zero end one period earlier.
Correct. Eight periods make one second; the last timestamp is seven periods after zero.

workedExample:
```formula
D = 8 / (8 / s) = 1 s
S = 7 / (8 / s) = 0.875 s
where
D: record duration, in seconds (s)
S: first-to-last timestamp span, in seconds (s)
s: second, the unit of time
In words: The record interval lasts one second without containing a sample at its excluded endpoint.
```

prompt: Which statements are valid for a uniformly sampled record? Select all that apply.

options.text: The sample rate must accompany a bare list
options.explanation: Correct. Values alone do not identify their time spacing.

options.text: An empty record has a zero first-to-last span
options.explanation: There is no first or last timestamp in an empty record, so that span is undefined.

options.text: A one-sample record has zero timestamp span
options.explanation: Correct. Its first and last timestamps are the same.

workedExample:
1. Separate the values from their timing metadata.
2. A non-empty record has a first and last timestamp.
3. With one sample these coincide; with no samples neither exists.
